transcript: Last night I was at the first preview of my window, an autobiographical show by Melissa Etheridge featuring her own music. I actually knew nothing about Melissa Etheridge before seeing his performance, so I'm probably not the target audience, but actually really enjoyed it, and it was like watching a memoir. Melissa basically tells her life story up to this point. She touches on growing up in Kansas, being queer enough, getting relationships, having children, and coping with sickness and loss, among other things. Her anecdotes help contextualize the songs, and I really like learning about musicians and what inspires their music, so I thought it was a really cool combination of narrative and music. The production design itself was also very cool. Had a lot of projections, and Melissa played multiple instruments, occasionally sound looping over herself. And overall, Melissa Ethridge is really, really good, and she gave an incredibly intimate performance. I particularly enjoyed her piano ballads. There's really no bad seat at the circle in the Square Theater where this is running, so I would definitely recommend going if you're a Melissa fan or even if you're just intrigued by this type of non traditional, intimate, autobiographical storytelling that we don't often get from singer songwriters, let alone rock stars. With that, another playbill for my collection.
